Generate Detection History and Covariate Matrices from camtrapDP Formatted Data

Source: R/matrix_generator.R
matrix_generator.Rd

This function processes camera trapping data formatted using the camtrapDP data standard to generate detection history matrices along with site-level and observation-level covariate matrices. These outputs can then be used for hierarchical occupancy or abundance modeling (e.g., with the unmarked package).

Usage

matrix_generator(
  obs,
  covs,
  dur,
  w,
  site_covs,
  obs_covs,
  all_locationNames,
  scientificNames,
  type,
  individuals,
  cap_count = FALSE
)

Arguments

obs

A data.frame of observations. This must include columns for date-time information (e.g., eventStart, eventEnd, a species identifier (scientificName), and a unique identifier for sampling units (e.g., cellID_10km in spatially resampled data from WildObsR::resample_covariates_and_observations() or deploymentID in regular camtrap DP data).

covs

A data.frame of covariates. This must include sampling start/end dates (e.g., samplingStart, samplingEnd in spatially resampled data from WildObsR::resample_covariates_and_observations() or deploymentStart, deploymentEnd in regular camtrap DP data), spatial identifiers (matching obs), and additional site-level covariate columns.

dur

A numeric value indicating the maximum sampling duration (in days) where a population is assumed to be closed to changes in size.

w

A numeric value specifying the length (in days) of each sampling occasion window that is used to compress the detection history matrix to improve model performance by increasing detection probability.

site_covs

A character vector of column names in covs to be used as site-level covariates.

obs_covs

A character vector of column names in obs to be used as observation-level covariates.

all_locationNames

A logical indicating whether all locationName values should be included (TRUE) or only locationNames with species detections (FALSE) should be included.

scientificNames

A character vector of species names to generate matrices for. Each species will be processed separately.

type

A character string indicating the type of model. Use "abundance" to generate a count history matrix using count data or "occupancy" to generate a detection history matrix using presence/absence data.

individuals

A character string specifying the method for aggregating individual counts used in the count history matrix. Use "sum" to sum detections across occasions or "max" to take the maximum value.

cap_count

Logical. If TRUE, the function will automatically cap observed counts for each species based on its mean and maximum observed group size to prevent extremely large counts from negatively affecting model fit. Species with high mean or maximum individual counts will have their values capped (e.g., at 3, 5, or 7), while others retain full counts. Default is FALSE, meaning no capping is applied.

Value

A named list where each element corresponds to a species. Each element is itself a list with the following components:

detection_matrix

A matrix of detection (or count) data with rows representing sampling units and columns representing sampling occasion windows.

site_level_covariates

A data.frame of site-level covariates used in the analysis.

observation_level_covariates

A list of matrices containing observation-level covariate, where each matrix is aligned with the detection history matrix.

Details

The function performs several key steps:

  1. Data Validation: Checks are performed to ensure that:

    • The identifier column (e.g., cellID or deploymentID) is consistent across obs and covs.

    • Every sampling unit in obs has a row in covs, and every observation covariate is a column of obs; otherwise the function stops.

    • NA values in site-level or observation-level covariates are kept, with a warning: unmarked drops the affected sampling units or occasions with its own warning.

    • Date-time columns in both obs and covs are POSIXct. Text columns are converted, with a message; a value that cannot be read stops the function.

    • No site-level covariate is dropped. One with the same value everywhere is kept, standardised to 0 if numeric.

    • The provided species names (scientificNames) exist in the obs table.

    Sampling units with covariates but no observations are kept, and enter every species' matrices as sampled zeros, with a message naming them.

  2. Timezone Adjustment: Date-time values are put in the local time zone of the sampling units, looked up from their coordinates with lutz::tz_lookup_coords, so records fall on their local day. When the sampling units span time zones with different clocks, every unit uses UTC days instead, with a message.

  3. Date Sequence and Sampling Occasions: A complete sequence of dates is generated for each sampling unit and an index is assigned to each sampling occasion.

  4. Matrix Generation: For each species, a detection history matrix is created by aligning observations to their respective sampling occasions. The matrix can contain either count data (for abundance models) or binary presence/absence data (for occupancy models).

  5. Observation-level Covariate Formatting: Observation covariates are organized into matrices that align with the detection history matrix and are compressed to match sampling occasion windows.

Known limitations

These come from how the inputs are built, and are why effort_matrix, detection_matrix and model_matrix_input exist. Prefer them for new analyses.

  • Effort depends on detections. numberDeploymentsActiveAtDate from resample_covariates_and_observations counts the deployments with a record that day, and a day without any record counts as one camera. Used as an observation covariate, it understates effort where several cameras share a sampling unit and varies with what was detected. matrix_generator() warns when it is used. effort_matrix calculates camera-days from the deployments alone.

  • Observation covariates come from the species' own records. On a day the species was detected, a covariate takes the values of the cameras that detected it; on other days, every value recorded at the sampling unit. So the covariate differs between detection and non-detection occasions for reasons unrelated to detection. model_matrix_input builds observation covariates from the deployments, weighted by camera-days.

  • Character observation covariates are pasted together (for example "none - trail") where several values meet, and summarised by their most common value per occasion, so they enter models as many-level factors.

  • A sampling unit is assumed to run continuously from its first start to its last end, so gaps between deployments in a cell count as sampled days.

See also

effort_matrix, detection_matrix and model_matrix_input, which build effort from deployments and format the result for unmarked, spOccupancy and spAbundance.

Author

Zachary Amir

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example usage with pre-processed camera trap data, accessed from WildObs:

# Load the general use WildObs API key
api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")
# use WildObsR function to access data
dp <- WildObsR::wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001")
# extract first DP from the list
dp <- dp[[1]]

# Extract resources from the data package
covs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "covariates")
obs  <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")
deps <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")

# Assign spatial scales
# 'scales' defines the area (in square meters) covered by the hexagonal cell
scales <- c(1000000, 3000000)

# Generate spatial hexagons based on the provided scales
covs <- WildObsR::spatial_hexagon_generator(covs, scales)

# Identify matching columns between deployments and covariates
cols <- names(deps)[names(deps) %in% names(covs)]
# Merge deployment information to the covariates
covs <- merge(deps, covs, by = cols)  # Note: This overwrites the original covs data

# Define columns for mode aggregation (example: 'projectName' and 'habitat')
mode_cols_covs <- names(covs)[grepl("projectName|habitat", names(covs))]
# Set the method for aggregating the total number of individuals detected:
individuals <- "sum"  # Alternative: "max"
# Specify observation-level covariate variables derived from deployments.
# These variables capture information that varies in space and time.
obs_covs <- c("baitUse", "featureType", "setupBy", "cameraModel", "cameraDelay","cameraHeight", "cameraDepth", "cameraTilt", "cameraHeading", "detectionDistance", "deploymentTags")

# now spatially resample the data, noting that this function may take a few minutes to run
resamp_data = WildObsR::resample_covariates_and_observations(covs, obs, individuals = "sum", mode_cols_covs, obs_covs)

# Select the resampled observations and covs at the 1 km scale
resamp_obs = resamp_data$spatially_resampled_observations$cellID_1km
resamp_covs = resamp_data$spatially_resampled_covariates$cellID_1km

# Run the matrix generator function
res <- matrix_generator(
  obs = resamp_obs,
  covs = resamp_covs,
  dur = 110,
  w = 3,
  site_covs = c("mode_habitat", "Avg_human_footprint_10km2", "locationName", "Avg_FLII_3km2"),
  obs_covs = c("cameraHeight", "featureType", "cameraModel"),
  all_locationNames = TRUE,
  scientificNames = c("Orthonyx spaldingii", "Uromys caudimaculatus"),
  type = "abundance",
  individuals = "sum"
)
# Access the detection matrix for one species:
res[["Orthonyx_spaldingii"]][["detection_matrix"]]
} # }
